sources.title: Kéré Architecture: Gando Primary School

sources.title: Right Livelihood: Yacouba Sawadogo
sources.note: Laureate profile: improved zaï, stone bunds, bird water pots and seed markets; checked full text.

sources.title: UNESCO: Royal Court of Tiébélé
sources.note: 2024 World Heritage inscription; synthesis describes house plans, inhabitants, materials and women’s mural knowledge.

sources.title: FESPACO, Burkina Faso’s contribution to UNESCO’s 2021 Luanda Biennale
sources.note: Member-state account hosted by UNESCO, not an independent UNESCO endorsement; 2021 festival dates and institutional description.

sources.title: UNICEF: Solar power facilitates access to water in the Sahel
sources.note: Myriam Dossou, 20 August 2024; Djeneba Dicko, Nafissa Sanou and Dori water facilities.

sources.title: Office of the Historian: Chad
sources.note: Recognition on 11 August 1960; Fort Lamy embassy and evacuation during 1980 fighting.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch: Chad’s ex-dictator convicted of atrocities
sources.note: Contemporaneous report by organization involved in victims’ campaign; 30 May 2016 conviction and 1982 to 1990 rule.

sources.title: House of Commons Library: Chad, prospects after the 2021 election
sources.note: 2021 briefing on Idriss Déby’s death and the military council headed by his son.

sources.title: Constitution of Chad, 2023
sources.note: WHO-hosted text, Articles 1, 8 and 10, PDF pages 5 and 6.

sources.title: Brunet and colleagues: New material of the earliest hominid from Chad, Nature, 2005
sources.note: Research abstract: TM 266 cranium, jaw and teeth, approximately seven million years; discovery and interpretation distinguished.

sources.title: Vignaud and colleagues: Geology and palaeontology of Toros-Menalla, Nature, 2002
sources.note: Research abstract: six specimens at TM 266; associated fauna and inferred lake, forest and savannah setting.

sources.title: Schelling and colleagues: Human and animal vaccination delivery to remote nomadic families, 2007
sources.note: Primary study abstract, programmes in Chad from 2000 to 2005; shared logistics and measured vaccination reach.

sources.title: Evaluation of joint human and animal vaccination in Danamadji, 2021
sources.note: Primary mixed-methods study: community acceptability, financial sustainability and infrastructure constraints.

sources.title: FAO: The Future Is an Ancient Lake, Atroun and Dihé
sources.note: Printed pages 274 to 285; harvest process and field notes of 10 to 11 March 2002. Historical health claims not repeated as medical facts.

sources.title: UNESCO: Guruna among the Massa
sources.note: 2025 joint Chad/Cameroon inscription; teaching, cattle, camp roles and performance.

sources.title: UNICEF: Accelerating school reopening in Chad, 11 May 2021
sources.note: Two-page primary case study; Lafya comic title and translation, distance learning and handwashing supplies.

sources.title: Office of the Historian: Burundi
sources.note: 1 July 1962 independence as a kingdom, following Belgian-administered UN trusteeship.

sources.title: Burundi Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Histoire
sources.note: Official indexed chronology checked; direct fetch timed out. Used narrowly for 28 November 1966 abolition, without adopting its political honorifics.

sources.title: Burundi tourism administration: Histoire et Culture
sources.note: Treaty of Kiganda section, 6 June 1903: Mwezi Gisabo and German sovereignty; official heritage account.

sources.title: UN Security Council welcomes Burundi’s transitional government, 2001
sources.note: Background on 1993 assassination and war; Arusha agreement of 28 August 2000, with fighting still continuing in 2001.

sources.title: Burundi constitution promulgated on 7 June 2018
sources.note: Official bilingual Kirundi/French document; indexed cover text checked. PDF fetch succeeds but extractor returns no lines. Sample is the cover heading, with French translation alongside.

sources.title: Burundi National Commission for UNESCO: Royal Residence of Gishora
sources.note: State-party tentative-list submission, 3 February 2026, not a World Heritage inscription. Description, architectural structure and drum sanctuary.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ritual dance of the royal drum
sources.note: 2014 inscription: ensemble organization, teaching and community gatherings.

sources.title: UNICEF: Growth monitoring in Ruyigi, 15 November 2022
sources.note: Odette Kwizera’s reporting: trained Light Mothers, equipment, home visits and nutritional counselling. Obvious age typo in English not repeated.

sources.title: UNICEF: Supporting health and school hygiene, 8 October 2025
sources.note: Jean Gabriel Uwamahoro; Gashoho Health Center and Kagari School. Distinguish latrines under construction from completed provision.

sources.title: Office of the Historian: Central African Republic
sources.note: Recognition and independence, 13 August 1960, after French rule.

sources.title: US State Department: Central African Republic background note, April 2004
sources.note: Official indexed historical text checked; direct fetch technical difficulties. Used for Bokassa’s 1976 empire and French-backed overthrow in 1979.

sources.title: MINUSCA: Overview and historical background
sources.note: Historical 2014 account: December 2012 rebellion, March 2013 seizure of Bangui and 2014 UN mission; old population estimates not used.

sources.title: William J. Samarin: Sango generic noun phrases, APiCS Online
sources.note: Introductory note gives Boganda’s exact slogan zo kwe zo and translation, and notes an early stamp. Sample follows this scholarly transcription, not an independently inspected stamp.

sources.title: UNESCO: Polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies of Central Africa
sources.note: Official source title retained; public prose uses Aka. 2003 proclamation/2008 inscription, vocal structure, instruments and childhood transmission.

sources.title: UNICEF: L’accès à l’eau donne l’espoir aux habitants de Bangui
sources.note: Jose Carlos Rodriguez Soto, 7 May 2025: Irène’s 2023 connection and Benisia’s breakfast stall.

sources.title: UNICEF: Raising Hopes with eduTrac in CAR
sources.note: Ye Ra Kim, 5 January 2016; launch December 2015, SMS reporting and practical rollout difficulties.

sources.title: El-Khatib and colleagues: SMS disease surveillance pilot in CAR, 2018
sources.note: Primary study, 21 health centres, 15 weeks in 2016. Uses methods/results and connectivity arrangements; avoids internal December 2016 pre-pilot typo.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Gabon
sources.note: Recognition account records independence on 17 August 1960 and the preceding French Equatorial African administration.

sources.title: Commonwealth Observer Group: Gabon Presidential Election, 12 April 2025
sources.note: Read political context, printed pages 21 to 24, and results, page 85. Use dated findings; several incidental dates in the report contain typographical errors and are not repeated.

sources.title: Gabon: Constitution of 19 December 2024, Journal officiel
sources.note: Official indexed PDF, Journal officiel no. 47 bis, page 1, Article Premier. The exact French motto is visible in the primary-source search extraction; direct PDF retrieval failed.

sources.title: IAEA: Meet Oklo, the Earth’s two-billion-year-old only known natural nuclear reactor
sources.note: Laura Gil, 10 August 2018. Describes the 1972 discovery, isotopic anomaly, geological age and water-mediated natural fission.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda
sources.note: Description and outstanding universal value: settlements, ironworking and approximately 1,800 petroglyphs along the Ogooué corridor.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Male Reliquary Figure (Nlo Bieri), 1979.206.119
sources.note: Catalogue identifies Gabon, Fang peoples, nineteenth to twentieth century, wood and palm oil; essay explains bark reliquaries and ancestral relationships.

sources.title: Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné: Clinical research
sources.note: Institutional account of RTS,S and GMZ2 vaccine trials, MIPPAD pregnancy study and clinical follow-up. Undated programme descriptions are not treated as a present-day patient count.

sources.title: UNICEF Gabon: Access to water, hygiene and sanitation in schools remains a priority
sources.note: September 2021 release reports June 2021 public-school sample survey, headteacher interviews, observations and SMS collection. Percentages describe surveyed schools.

sources.title: United Nations: Trusteeship Agreement for Togoland under French Administration
sources.note: Preamble and Article 1 identify the eastern territory, the boundary declaration of 10 July 1919 and the French mandate of 20 July 1922.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Togo
sources.note: Records independence and recognition on 27 April 1960, following French-administered UN trusteeship.

sources.title: US Department of State: Togo, 2005 human rights report
sources.note: Published 8 March 2006; opening and political-rights section describe Eyadema’s death and the contested succession.

sources.title: International IDEA: Togo democracy tracker
sources.note: Country background and May 2025 development: new parliamentary system and Faure Gnassingbé as President of the Council of Ministers.

sources.title: Togo National Assembly: Constitution of 6 May 2024
sources.note: Official Journal no. 42 bis, Article 2. Official PDF indexed but direct retrieval failed; full Article 2 also checked in the contemporary newspaper reproduction hosted at https://www.republicoftogo.com/content/download/113985/2935970/1, PDF page 3.

sources.title: UNESCO: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba
sources.note: Outstanding universal value and authenticity explain the shared Benin/Togo landscape, earthen tower-houses, ground-floor animal spaces, terrace granaries and living traditions.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum: Fabric of the African Diaspora
sources.note: Museum essay identifies cloth designs, Togolese trader Madame Santa Anna Nelly and Nana Benz trade networks.

sources.title: WHO: Togo eliminates trachoma as a public health problem
sources.note: 28 May 2022. Distinguishes elimination as a public-health problem from worldwide eradication; describes hygiene, water and continued monitoring.

sources.title: WHO and UNICEF: State of the World’s Sanitation, 2020
sources.note: Box 7, Improving sanitation in schools in Togo: 44 percent in 2016 to 65 percent in 2019, school-led work and gender-separated facilities.

sources.title: UNICEF Togo: Country Office Annual Report 2021
sources.note: Page 9: 14 family and five school biogas latrines; biodigesters, cooking fuel, digestate and household financing.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: South Sudan
sources.note: Summary and recognition sections: 2005 peace agreement, January 2011 referendum and independence on 9 July 2011.

sources.title: United Nations Mission in South Sudan: Factsheet
sources.note: Describes the December 2013 crisis and the 2014 reorientation of the mission toward civilian protection.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General: Statement on South Sudan, 13 September 2018
sources.note: Records the 12 September 2018 revitalized agreement and calls for full implementation, not an assertion that all violence had ended.

sources.title: UN Peacekeeping: South Sudan on the brink as peace deal falters
sources.note: 16 April 2025 UN briefing report; official full indexed extraction read, direct retrieval returned 403. Dated warning of renewed confrontation.

sources.title: Manfredi and Petrollino, APiCS Online: Juba Arabic, want-complement subjects
sources.note: Example 64-197, attributed to Manfredi 2005, page 170: exact Latin-letter transcription and English translation. The online atlas is a scholarly record, not an ancient manuscript or an official national spelling.

sources.title: Rift Valley Institute: National Archive of South Sudan
sources.note: Project participant’s account of damaged records, conservation and the November 2017 Tarikh Tana radio series. Current-building and digitization completion claims are not inferred from this older account.

sources.title: UNICEF: Getting girls back to the classroom after COVID-19 school closures
sources.note: Education case study, 11 March 2021, page 2: Torit toilets and handwashing, mothers’ groups and girls’ leadership.

sources.title: UNICEF: Inauguration of solar-powered water supply system in Yei
sources.note: 30 May 2023 release gives five boreholes, 59 kiosks, 33 kilometres of pipe and chlorination. Describes opening specifications, not guaranteed later functioning.

sources.title: UNICEF: How solarization is attaining results in Boma
sources.note: Garang Abraham Malak, 9 May 2023. Late-2022 installation, staff Betty Anying and Allan Ngoray, lighting and vaccine storage. Do not infer sole causation for mortality improvements.

sources.title: United Nations in South Sudan: Spreading Hope Through Women’s Empowerment, Veronica’s Story
sources.note: 2025 first-person programme reporting from Mangaten: 21-year-old interpreter and student, psychosocial support, soap and basket-making.

sources.title: FIBA: Unforgettable first, South Sudan overcomes Puerto Rico with team effort
sources.note: Official Paris 2024 game report: 90 to 79 first Olympic victory, Nuni Omot first points, Carlik Jones and rebounding statistics.
